title: R' Avdimi, Brother of R' Yose (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [In the fourth generation in the Land of Israel.] He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:2, Kilayim 6:4 and Shabbat 2:5. In Hyman’s retelling of Bava Batra 2:3, R’ Acha became angry with him and he fell ill. His brother R’ Assi went up to visit him, thought him near death and arranged shrouds for him. Afterwards he recovered.

notes.text: The heading calls him Yose’s brother, while the supplied body names Assi as his brother and visitor. The complete Bava Batra2:3 paragraph names Yose; its compressed shroud account also differs in detail from the notice’s retelling. These remain source questions.

The saved whole Venice BavaBatra2:3 scalar repeatedly calls Avdumi Yose’s brother and explicitly has Yose visit. This supports the heading’s Yose, while supplied body Assi remains translated as supplied. The court-compassion/shroud ending does not explicitly verify every near-death and recovery detail of Hyman’s retelling. Avdimi/Avdumi, fourth-generation dating and the other citations are not silently reconciled. Personal titles in this Venice scalar are abbreviated; the exact full Rabbi expansions are withdrawn, without changing identity or classification.

Hyman’s printed heading names R’ Yose as Avdimi’s brother, while the body gives R’ Assi as the brother who visits. Both the consulted Venice and Guggenheimer texts of Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 2:3 call him Avdumi and name Yose as the visitor. They close with a terse exchange about the court and shrouds. Hyman’s account adds the near-death expectation and recovery. The other three cited passages also call him Yose’s brother, with variations in the spelling of Avdimi.
